schema: Compact authoring format. Imported by backend/app/datasets/importers/manufacturer_docs.py into the unified RepairRecord schema. Every entry paraphrases one source in sources.json. Nothing here is invented: if a source does not state a cause or check, the field stays empty.

symptoms: CH04 or FL shown on display
water not draining from indoor unit
faults: Condensate water is not draining from the indoor unit
Indoor drain fault or full condensate tank (ceiling units)
High humidity or rain increasing condensate (window/portable units)
checks: Switch off at the plug or breaker, wait 5 minutes, restore power
For window or portable units, drain condensate from the rear drain port into a container
entries.action: Power-cycle first. If the code returns after a reset, or recurs often on dry days, the drain needs a technician inspection.

symptoms: indoor and outdoor unit not communicating
faults: Communication error between indoor and outdoor unit
Often follows installation or relocation, or unstable power
checks: Power-cycle the unit (off 5 minutes)
If it started after installation or relocation, contact the installer
entries.action: Power-cycle. Request service if it persists. On some models E0 only means kW Manager is running.

symptoms: CH07 shown on multi-unit or 2-in-1 system
faults: Connected units set to conflicting modes (one heating while another cools or dehumidifies)
checks: Check the mode of every connected unit
entries.action: Set all units to heating, or all to cooling/dehumidification. Fan and air-purification modes can run at any time.

faults: Refrigerant shortage or piping connection fault after installation or relocation
checks: If installed or relocated recently, contact the installer
During normal use, power-cycle once
entries.action: If it reappears after a power cycle, piping and refrigerant need a technician. Refrigerant work is for certified technicians only.

symptoms: CH54 shown after a power cut or electrical work
faults: Reverse phase detected in the supply
checks: Reset the AC circuit breaker
Ask whether electrical work was done recently
entries.action: If it follows electrical work, the electrician must correct the phase wiring. Inspect if it persists.

faults: Outdoor unit overheating during cooling (poor ventilation, enclosed balcony)
Indoor unit overheating during heating (dirty filter, blocked intake)
checks: Open balcony vents and clear space around the outdoor unit
Check the outdoor unit discharge is aligned with the opening; an air guide can help
Clean the indoor filter
entries.action: Fix ventilation, then power-cycle (the code does not clear on its own). Inspect if it persists.

faults: Communication or piping connection fault between units
checks: Power-cycle (about 5 minutes)
Contact the installer if it began after installation
entries.action: Request inspection if it persists after a power cycle.

faults: Debris caught in the indoor fan
checks: With power off, look for visible debris around the indoor fan
entries.action: Remove visible debris. If nothing is visible or the code persists, request service.

faults: Debris caught in the outdoor fan
checks: With power off, look for debris around the outdoor fan
entries.action: Remove visible debris. If nothing is visible or the code persists, request service.

symptoms: CH90 or CH91 shown during test run
faults: Test-run protection: piping connection problem after installation
checks: After installation, have the installer check piping
During use, power-cycle
entries.action: Service if it persists after a power cycle.

faults: On 2021-onward models, the outdoor unit may not be powered
checks: Check the outdoor unit plug is in a wall socket (not a power strip) and its breaker is on
Check cable connections, then power-cycle
entries.action: Request service if it persists after these checks.

symptoms: AC not starting on a model with separate outdoor power cord
faults: Outdoor unit has no power: plug disconnected or breaker off
checks: Plug the outdoor unit directly into a wall outlet, not an extension
Confirm the outdoor breaker is on
entries.action: Do not reset a breaker repeatedly if it will not stay on; request service.

faults: Temporary fault from power instability or other electrical factors
checks: Unplug or switch off the breaker, wait about 5 minutes, restore power
entries.action: If it persists, the unit needs a technician inspection.

faults: Faulty or loose temperature or pipe sensor
checks: Unplug or switch off the breaker, wait about 5 minutes, restore power, see if the code clears
entries.action: If the code clears and the unit runs normally it can be used. If it returns, stop using it and request service. Do not disassemble or replace internal parts yourself.
safety: Do not disassemble or replace internal parts yourself: risk of fire, electric shock or death.

faults: Compressor drive or protection circuit error
Faulty electrical component in the outdoor unit
checks: Unplug or switch off the breaker, wait about 5 minutes, restore power
entries.action: If the code returns after reset, stop using the unit and request service.
safety: Do not disassemble or replace internal parts yourself: risk of fire, electric shock or death.

checks: Check breaker or fuse
Check the plug
Check for a power cut
Check remote batteries
Check timer settings

faults: Low fan speed or airflow direction
checks: Check set temperature and mode
Check fan speed and airflow direction
Clean the air filters
Remove obstructions near indoor and outdoor units
Close doors and windows

faults: Inlet or outlet of indoor or outdoor unit blocked
checks: Clean the air filters and restart from the remote
Remove anything blocking inlets or outlets
entries.action: If the lamp still flashes, switch off at the breaker and contact the place of purchase.

checks: Stop operation and switch off at the plug or breaker
entries.action: Daikin advises contacting the place of purchase for a water leak from the indoor unit.

faults: Odours absorbed in the room released by the indoor unit
Very small amount of ozone from streamer operation (not a health hazard per Daikin)

checks: Switch off and unplug, remove the front panel, vacuum or wash the filter, let it dry fully, refit
entries.action: Samsung recommends cleaning the filter about every 2 weeks.

checks: Confirm mode and temperature (Cool/Auto/Heat 16-30 C, Dry 18-30 C; Fan mode has no temperature)
Replace remote batteries with two new AAA cells

faults: Other appliances on the same circuit
Fault in the unit or wiring if trips are frequent
checks: Check and reset the breaker
Unplug other appliances on the same circuit
entries.action: Frequent trips may mean a fault in the unit or wiring: consult a professional technician.

symptoms: AC not cooling after other checks
checks: Rule out filter, settings and power first
entries.action: Low refrigerant needs professional servicing; contact Samsung support.

faults: Condensation from a very low set temperature and high humidity
checks: Raise the set temperature (Samsung suggests 24 C)
Run Dry mode for 3-4 hours, then return to Cool
Set fan speed to medium or high
entries.action: If leakage continues, contact Samsung customer care for an engineer visit.

checks: Collect the water in a container while checking
Check the drain pipe slope and correct it
Clean the air filter

faults: Loose plug or socket, or wall switch off
checks: Confirm there is no power cut
Check the plug is seated and the wall switch is on
Test the socket with another appliance
Check for a grounded three-wire connection and a stable 230 V / 50 Hz supply
entries.action: Use a dedicated wall socket, no extension cords or multi-plugs. If the socket is dead, call an electrician. If still no power, contact a Samsung service centre.
safety: Do not disassemble or repair the refrigerator yourself.
escalate: Still no power after socket checks

symptoms: direct cool fridge not cold enough
faults: Temperature knob not set for the season
Fridge overloaded so air cannot circulate
Shelf liners or mats blocking airflow
checks: Set the knob higher in summer (about 5-6), mid in monsoon (3-4), lower in winter (1-2), per the model manual
Remove excess items and leave gaps
Use only supplied shelves; remove liners
Open the door less often

faults: Heavy ice build-up from missed manual defrosting
checks: Press the defrost button and let all ice melt
Defrost regularly (Samsung suggests about twice a week, or when ice is heavy)

faults: Not enough clearance from walls or installed in an enclosed space
Sides covered with cloth or panels so heat cannot escape
Door gasket damaged or not seated evenly
checks: Leave clearance around the fridge
Remove side coverings
Inspect the gasket for gaps or damage
entries.action: If cooling does not improve, contact a Samsung service centre. Do not repair internal components yourself.

faults: Normal operation: refrigerant flow, defrost water on the heater, valve clicking, plastic expanding, compressor and fan running faster after door opening
checks: Confirm the fridge is cooling normally
entries.action: No action needed for these sounds.

faults: Fridge not level or touching wall or cabinet
checks: Leave clearance at back and sides
Adjust levelling legs
Move to a flat, solid floor if needed
safety: Use at least two people to move or level the refrigerator.

symptoms: fridge tapping or rattling from fan
checks: Move food to another fridge or cooler
Unplug and leave doors open until frost fully melts (about 24 hours in summer, up to 3 days in winter)
entries.action: If the noise returns, schedule a service visit.

faults: Temporary compressor or fan motor issue, or component needing service
checks: Check whether the fridge still cools normally
entries.action: If it cools normally, monitor. If the noise continues or cooling is poor, contact LG service.

faults: Door or drawer not fully closed
checks: Close doors and drawers fully and move items blocking them
Check the breaker in the distribution board and reset it
entries.action: If the breaker trips again, have an electrician check the circuit.

symptoms: fan not running but light works
checks: With power isolated, check the fan switch for continuity with a multimeter
Inspect switch wiring
entries.action: Replace a faulty switch or tighten connections.

checks: With power isolated, test the fuse for continuity
entries.action: Replace the fuse if there is no continuity.

faults: Loose or worn wiring from poor installation or age
checks: With power isolated and verified, inspect connections for looseness or damage
entries.action: Tighten or repair connections; replace damaged wiring.

symptoms: fan does not start but has power
fan hums but does not spin
checks: With power isolated, inspect the capacitor, motor and internal wiring
entries.action: Replace the faulty component, or call a technician for motor faults.

symptoms: fan runs only at some speeds
checks: Check regulator and capacitor first, then wiring
entries.action: Replace defective parts; call a professional if the motor is worn.

checks: Look for dust build-up
Check supply stability
entries.action: Clean blades, lubricate bearings, replace a weak capacitor, or stabilise the supply.

checks: Inspect all screws and blade alignment
entries.action: Tighten fittings, align blades, or use a balancing kit.

checks: Find the source; check fittings and blades
entries.action: Tighten, clean and lubricate; get the fan serviced if noise persists.

checks: Let the motor cool before handling or restarting
With power isolated, inspect electrical components
entries.action: Fix the underlying electrical fault before restarting. Have the supply checked after surges.
safety: Let the motor cool before handling.
Call a professional for motor or electrical faults.

faults: Reverse or wall switch in the wrong position
checks: Check breaker, fuse, reverse switch, wall switch and remote batteries
entries.action: Reset the breaker or replace the fuse. Frayed wiring needs an electrician.

faults: Mounted on a box not rated for the fan's weight
checks: Check fasteners, blade condition and mounting box rating
entries.action: Tighten fasteners, replace damaged blades instead of bending them, use a fan-rated box.

checks: Check fasteners, blade balance and clearance around the blades
entries.action: On a new fan, allow about 24 hours for lubricant to spread. If noise persists, call an electrician or the manufacturer.

checks: With power isolated, test the capacitor with a multimeter
Check bearings, regulator and supply voltage
entries.action: Replace a faulty capacitor, clean bearings, repair the regulator, or replace a worn motor.

checks: With power isolated, check connections and the pull chain

faults: Motor overheating from long use, poor ventilation or wear
Dust overheating in motor or capacitor
checks: Switch the fan off and disconnect power immediately
Look for visible damage
entries.action: If it continues, consult a professional electrician to avoid a fire hazard.

checks: Leave the door slightly open after cooking and wipe the cavity dry

symptoms: steam or air escaping around microwave door
faults: Food or debris on the door seal
checks: Clean the gasket
Inspect the seal for damage
Check the door closes without gaps
entries.action: A damaged door or seal needs authorised service.

symptoms: microwave display works but will not start
faults: Door not fully closed or latched
Packing material or debris on the door seal
checks: Close the door firmly
Clear the door seal
Check the door for damage
Press Cancel (twice) and re-enter the settings

faults: Timer not set or Start not pressed
checks: Check the timer and press Start
Check the breaker or fuse

faults: Wrong time or power level for the food
checks: Set time by food type and weight
Choose the correct power level
Stir or turn food halfway

entries.action: Samsung says the lamp should not be replaced personally; it must be replaced by Samsung service.
safety: Do not replace the lamp yourself.

faults: Metal utensils, metal-trimmed dishes or twist ties inside
Foil too large or too close to the walls
checks: Stop the oven and remove all metal
Use only narrow foil strips at least one inch from the walls

symptoms: smoke or smell during first uses of a new microwave
faults: New components heating for the first time (normal per Samsung)
checks: Run empty for 10 minutes, or heat lemon slices or juice for 1 minute

symptoms: microwave interferes with TV or radio
faults: Electromagnetic emissions during operation (slight interference is normal)
checks: Move the oven away from TVs, radios and aerials
If the display resets, unplug, wait 10 seconds, plug back in

symptoms: microwave display blank and oven dead
faults: Not plugged into a grounded outlet
checks: Plug into a grounded outlet and switch it on
Unplug 10 seconds and replug
Reset breaker or replace fuse
Test the outlet with another appliance; try another outlet
entries.action: If another appliance also fails on that outlet, a qualified electrician must repair the outlet.

symptoms: microwave stops before the set time
checks: Let it cool about 30 minutes
Unplug for 10 seconds and plug back in
Check the outlet and power cord
entries.action: Damaged wiring or a breaker that trips with the oven unplugged needs service; electrical repairs only by a licensed electrician.

faults: Voltage drop from sharing a circuit with other appliances
checks: Run the oven on its own dedicated circuit

faults: Dirty turntable, roller ring or floor
Turntable or roller ring not seated
checks: Clean the turntable, roller ring and floor
Seat them correctly

symptoms: microwave runs but does not heat
faults: Demo mode is on (magnetron disabled for showroom display)
checks: Start a short cook and watch the timer
Disable demo mode from the Options or My Settings menu as the user manual describes
entries.action: If the model has no demo mode in its manual, contact Samsung support.

faults: Kitchen Timer selected instead of a cooking cycle
Very small food quantity heating unevenly
checks: Select a normal cooking cycle
Try a larger quantity

symptoms: microwave not heating or weak heat after installation
faults: Insufficient clearance so the oven cannot vent
checks: Compare left, right, top and rear clearances with the installation manual
entries.action: If none of the checks fix it, it may be a hardware fault: contact Samsung service.

checks: Clean the storage tank
Discard old water
entries.action: Filter replacement by an authorised Eureka Forbes technician.

checks: Open the inlet valve
Check tap pressure
entries.action: If low output persists or filters are suspected, call an authorised technician.

symptoms: water not flowing into purifier storage tank
checks: Check the overhead tank has water
Open the supply tap
entries.action: If the cause is unclear, call an authorised technician.

symptoms: water leaking from top of purifier
checks: Close the tap water valve and unplug the power cord
entries.action: Call an authorised Eureka Forbes service technician.

symptoms: purifier stuck in standby after water supply returns
purifier stops when water supply fails
faults: Dry run sensor stopped the pump because there was no input water
checks: Switch the power off and on once supply is back
entries.action: The unit rechecks for water at intervals; a power cycle restarts it if it stays in standby.

symptoms: poor output on loft tank or suction supply
faults: Input flow below the 1.5 LPM the pump needs
checks: Confirm inlet flow is above 1.5 LPM
Confirm the suction container is within 3 feet below the unit
entries.action: Eureka Forbes recommends an external booster pump if low input pressure prevents adequate flow. Do not reuse rejected water.

symptoms: no water flow when switched on
checks: Check water supply and mains supply
entries.action: If both are normal, call the Eureka Forbes service centre.

checks: Switch the unit off until voltage returns to normal
Open the supply valve
Check plug and power switch
Check whether the tank is full

symptoms: low water pressure from RO purifier
checks: Confirm inlet pressure
entries.action: If it persists, contact Kent support.

symptoms: grinding or loud noise from purifier
faults: Abnormal pump or component noise (normal pump hum during purification is not a fault)
checks: Switch the unit off immediately
entries.action: Contact Kent support.

checks: Shut off the main water supply and disconnect power
entries.action: Kent says not to fix it yourself; contact Kent support.
safety: Do not attempt to fix a leak yourself.

symptoms: purified water has bad taste or odour
checks: Check filter replacement dates
Check installation
entries.action: Replace filters; contact support if it continues.

checks: Check power
Open the inlet valve
Check household water pressure
entries.action: If filters are suspected, contact authorised service.

symptoms: slow water flow from purifier faucet
entries.action: Contact service to inspect or replace filters and check tank pressure.

symptoms: purified water smells or tastes bad
entries.action: Contact service to replace the filter and clean the tank.

checks: Check for a displayed error code
entries.action: Contact authorised service.

checks: Turn off water supply and power immediately
entries.action: Contact authorised service. Do not open or repair the purifier yourself.
safety: Do not open or repair the purifier yourself.
